name: radiating-block-transient
reference: Benchmark E7: a 1 mm cube, insulated on five faces, radiating as a black body from the sixth into a 0 K sink. Its conductivity is deliberately enormous (1e4 W/(m K), radiative Biot number 6e-6) so the cube stays isothermal and the answer is the lumped energy balance rho cp V dT/dt = -sigma eps A T^4, i.e. dT/dt = -c T^4 with c = sigma A / (rho cp V) = 5.670374419e-9 K^-3 s^-1 for A/V = 1/L, L = 1 mm, rho = 100 kg/m^3, cp = 100 J/(kg K). Separating variables gives the closed form T(t) = T0 (1 + 3 c T0^3 t)^(-1/3), which is 381.49284808810995 K at t = 1 s from T0 = 1000 K. A linearised film cannot reproduce a fourth-power decay by accident. Crank-Nicolson at dt = 5 ms lands 3.3e-5 relative from the closed form; the engine test halves the increment three times and measures the theta-method's own rates, 1 at theta = 1 and 2 at theta = 0.5.

checks.note: T(1 s) of the analytic fourth-power decay
